The base set

MKP ships no widgets of its own beyond these. Everything else, in a document or a pack, is composed from them. Each opens in the examples, alone, in its states.

#Layout

Widget What it does
column Children one below another: gap, padding, alignment, a border and a wash.
row Children side by side: alignment, wrapping, or scrolling sideways.
grid Children in columns: tracks such as [auto, 1fr], a cell spanning two.
stack Children drawn one over another, the last on top.

#Text and pictures

Widget What it does
text A run of inline Markdown: font, tone, weight, size, lines kept or clipped.
image A picture from the document's folder, with its description.
icon A symbol from a fixed set.

#Controls

Widget What it does
press Anything clickable: a button, a tab, a toggle, a switch, an answer row.
range A value on a track.
meter How far along something is.
field Text or number entry, marked right or wrong.
overlay A tooltip, popover, menu or dialog, anchored to what opens it.

#Drawing

Widget What it does
canvas A coordinate space in layers: paths, circles, labels, and handles the reader drags.

arrow from=a to=b joins two elements by id, and with gfx@1 a canvas also draws pixels and mesh.

#Markdown blocks

These are what Markdown itself becomes, so a document's prose is the base set too.

Widget What it does
paragraph A paragraph of inline Markdown.
heading Headings.
list Bulleted, numbered and task lists.
quote A quotation, and the five alerts.
code A code block, with a current line and marked lines.
math A display formula, with parts marked and noted.
divider A break between parts.
table A table of inline Markdown cells.
footnote A footnote and the mark that leads to it.

#The host's shell

Widget What it does
frame A widget's shell: title, actions, a status bar, drawers, full screen.
pane Titled columns that scroll on their own, side by side.
zoom A view the reader unlocks to zoom and pan.

#Composed from them

The examples also show everyday widgets built from the base set, each a few lines long: card, tabs, accordion, segmented, stat, stepper, badges, rating, checklist, pagination. Copy one as a start.
